result: The authors describe a collection of 3060 adult and 1373 larval split-GAL4 lines resulting from screening over 77,000 hemidriver combinations. All lines were rescreened with standardized imaging of male and female samples to confirm expression patterns.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the collection's scope and scale, describing it as a 'significant increment' and noting that the lines have been 'thoughtfully curated and documented.' The editor states the evidence is 'convincing,' and no reviewer questions the numbers or validation methodology.

result: The collection was classified into quality levels based on specificity: 1767 lines with single cell-type expression (level 1), 1232 lines with two cell types (level 2), 26 lines with three or more cell types (level 3), and 34 lines with weak/variable expression (level 4).
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise the 'classification of line combination according to quality levels' as a strength that 'provides a relevant criterion while deciding to use a particular set of splits.' No concerns are raised about the classification system.

result: Male/female expression differences were observed in 109 of 3060 lines, with more female expression in the epaulette and abdominal ganglion, and more male expression in the antennal mechanosensory and motor center and mushroom body regions.
evaluation: Reviewers specifically highlight 'discrimination between male and female expression patterns' as a strength that provides 'hints regarding the potential role of these gender-specific circuits.' The editor notes the resource is valuable for 'understanding...differences between the sexes.'

result: The cell-type lines show broad CNS coverage, with 96% of voxels having expression from at least 5 lines. Prominently labeled areas include the fan-shaped body, lobula, and superior medial protocerebrum, while the antennal lobe is rarely labeled.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the spatial distribution analysis. They acknowledge the collection's utility for 'mapping of neuronal circuits' and note that the 'search engine seems to be user-friendly,' implicitly accepting the distribution data that enables such searches.

result: The collection has been deposited at Bloomington Drosophila Stock Center and made available through multiple online platforms including splitgal4.janelia.org, neuronbridge.janelia.org, and Virtual Fly Brain for searching and comparison.
evaluation: Reviewers praise the data availability and accessibility, noting 'the search engine seems to be user-friendly' and that the authors have made the lines 'maximally useful to the greater community.' No concerns are raised about data access.

result: The raw image collection includes 46,653 IS/SS combinations, 129,665 fly samples, 612,124 3D image stacks, and 4,371,364 processed outputs totaling 192 TB. About 77,000 IS crosses were examined, with 36,033 imaged and 8273 stabilized into SS lines.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the scale of the screening effort and praise the availability of 'some information from the other lines they created and tested but deemed not specific or strong enough to be included' as 'a valuable aid.' No concerns are raised about these quantitative claims.

result: The larval collection includes 982 split-GAL4 lines, 31 Generation 1 GAL4 lines, and 353 Generation 1 LexA lines, selected to have no more than 2 neurons per brain hemisphere or VNC hemisegment.
evaluation: Reviewers praise the 'description of expression patterns in the adult and larvae, expanding the audience for these tools' as a strength. The editor notes the resource is valuable for understanding expression patterns 'in adults and larvae.' No concerns are raised about the larval collection.

result: The authors acknowledge multiple caveats: many lines have off-target expression, effector strength varies, transvection can occur, expression varies with development, not all lines have cell-type information, biological variability exists, and specific lines have not been developed for every CNS cell type. They estimate creating precise lines for one-third of cell types, imprecise lines for another third, and no usable line for the remaining third.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise 'an acknowledgement of the caveats and challenges that splits (like any other genetic tool) can carry' and note that 'added revisions help to clarify...caveats to be mindful of when using any of the described lines.' One reviewer states 'my concerns were resolved regarding the existence of caveats.' The limitation that 'lines that are part of this specific collection are sparse and specific but also limited in which cell types they cover' is acknowledged as both a strength and weakness.

result: Specific example lines are presented showing expression in characterized cell types including P-FNv neurons (SS52577), PAM-α1 dopaminergic neurons (MB043C), 8B(t1) cholinergic neurons (SS40265), wing neuropil ascending neurons (SS60203), LBL40 neurons mediating backwards walking (SS47938), and DNg34 (SS72207).
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge any specific line examples. They note the lines are 'thoughtfully curated and documented' with 'confocal images of neurons labeled by each driver line and when possible, a list of cell types labeled.' The examples serve to illustrate the collection's utility.

result: The authors provide background on the split-GAL4 system and its development, including the limitations of earlier Generation 1 GAL4 lines (less than 1% single cell-type specific), the split-GAL4 mechanism, screening success rates (1-2% single cell-type specific), and recent advances in computational search tools and EM datasets that facilitated line generation.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the historical context or technical background. They acknowledge the manuscript 'follows the same experimental pipeline described before' and represents a continuation of established methods. The background claims are well-supported by citations and accepted without challenge.

result: The Janelia FlyLight Project has contributed 540,000 3D images of 230,000 fly CNS samples in total, and stocks have been distributed 300,000 times to thousands of groups in over 50 countries.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the broad impact and utility of the resource, noting it 'will be of broad interest to Drosophila researchers' and represents 'the cooperation of several labs throughout the Drosophila community.' The distribution statistics support the resource's value.

result: Methodological details are provided including fly rearing conditions (21-25°C, 50% humidity), dissection timing (1-5 days for rescreening), image alignment to JRC2018 template, and segmentation yielding 10,778 brain and 9310 VNC objects after filtering.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the methodological details. They note 'added revisions help to clarify important points relating to the creation of the lines' and that the documentation increases 'the manuscript's utility to users.' The methods are accepted as appropriate.
